messages:
nina: Quick sync: following the dashboard-query RFC, I'm proposing a "query-protection shim" in front of the console query service to avoid expensive RBAC-driven scans taking down the cluster. Sketching options & tradeoffs here.

omar: high-level: is the shim an authz-aware proxy or an emergency throttle layer?

nina: both, ideally. primary job is to detect pathological patterns and route to cheaper execution plans (materialized windows, rollups, or sampled answers). secondary job is soft-authz checks to avoid full-table joins when possible.

sylvia: important: we can't weaken RBAC semantics. Any authz shortcuts must be provably safe. If we use pre-aggregates, they must be scoped to the smallest authz unit (tenant or role).

ethan: that implies a lot more cache keys. We should measure the expected cache blowup before committing. Could we instead keep full authz verification but short-circuit heavy joins with a pre-filter step? e.g., apply tenant filter early so join cardinality drops.

nina: good point. Two engineering paths: A) shim-only (config + feature flag) that applies routing & approximation without changing query runtime; B) invest in runtime authz pushdown (longer). Shim-only gives quick mitigation but higher cache cost.

omar: for user experience, we need a clear fallback messaging strategy. If an approximation is served, UI shows a compact banner: "Approximate results used due to load; refresh for exact" with link to explain mode. Ops must be able to disable approximation per-tenant.

sylvia: plus legal/compliance: some dashboards are not allowed to be approximated. We'll need route metadata to mark "no-approx".

ethan: policy engine idea: route metadata includes {priority, allow_approx, authz_complexity_hint}. Shim consults this and a deterministic scoring function to decide. Score inputs: cluster_cpu_pct, route_rps, tenant_active_percentile, authz_hint.

nina: proposal for weight defaults: cpu:0.45, rps:0.25, tenant_hot:0.2, authz:0.1. threshold triggers materialize/approx path. Also expose these weights as console config.

omar: ops wants observability: emit shim.decision with the input vector, chosen path, and whether authz passed/short-circuited. Keep for 72h.

sylvia: add deterministic request_id -> decision_trace so we can reproduce. Also ensure trace ids are preserved when switching paths.

ethan: perf test plan: synthetic mix of auth-heavy reports and ad-hoc filters. Measure 95th latency, CPU, cache_miss_rate for per-tenant keys vs global+delta design.

nina: rollout plan: 1) implement shim behind flag (console.query_protection.canary) with only rate-based routing; 2) enable per-route metadata hooks; 3) enable approximation modes for low-priority routes; 4) consider runtime authz pushdown RFC.

omar: do we have a safe rollback? For noisy tenants, add tenant-level kill-switch + global circuit-breaker. Document steps in playbook.

sylvia: UI: I'll draft the approximation banner language and a short help doc. Legal will review.

infra-bot: feature flag created: console.query_protection.canary (owners: @nina, @ethan).

nina: thanks. I'll write the follow-up RFC with config examples, test matrix, and playbook and link this thread.

ethan: happy to help with load harness & tracing.

omar: I'll run a cache projection and give numbers.

sylvia: +1 to draft RFC.

nina: will post the doc tomorrow and tag product/compliance. Thanks all for quick feedback.
